value.description: Text, or {"env": "NAME"}: read from IED's environment when the server starts, so no secret is written in a settings file.

command.description: A program on PATH or a path, started in the workspace and spoken to on its standard input and output (stdio). A .cmd or .bat (npx) runs through cmd.exe.

cwd.description: The folder it runs in, relative to the workspace root (the default).

url.description: A running server's streamable-HTTP endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp, or https:// (TLS: its certificate must chain to a root Windows trusts, or to caFile, and name the URL's host).

caFile.description: With an https url: a PEM (or DER) file of CA certificates its certificate may chain to besides the ones Windows trusts - a local or corporate authority. Relative to the workspace root. It never turns the check off.

permission.description: ask: every call of its tools asks you, in any permission mode, until you allow it for the chat (or an ai.permissions allow rule does); auto: its tools are commands that follow the chat's permission mode; read: you say it only reads - its tools run without asking and are offered in Plan mode.

preload.description: true, or names of its tools: send them whole with every request. Otherwise they are deferred (shown whole by tool_search).

privacy.description: Where what its tools are sent goes: local for a command or a loopback URL, cloud for any other URL unless said.

timeoutSeconds.description: How long a call may take before it is cancelled.

startSeconds.description: How long a start may take to answer initialize (uvx and npx may download the server on its first run).

exclude.description: Its tools left out, by the server's names.

mcp.servers.description: MCP servers whose tools the AI gets in a trusted workspace, by name: {command, args?, env?, cwd?} or {url, headers?, caFile?}, with enabled, permission, preload, privacy, timeoutSeconds, startSeconds and exclude (docs/04 MCP). A deeper tier's entry of a name replaces the one above it.

mcp.idleMinutes.description: A server no call used for this long is stopped; its tools stay offered and the next call starts it again. 0: it runs until IED stops.
